science.title: Urban Stressors Disrupt the Phenological Clock, Unravelling Urban Ecosystems and Services
science.description: Urban environments impose unique stressors, urban heat islands, artificial light at night, nitrogen deposition, and noise pollution, that disrupt the phenological rhythms of flora and fauna. Urban planning must shift from static greening to dynamic management of environmental cues. This Perspective synthesizes recent evidence, explores societal impacts, and proposes a temporally-aware framework integrating monitoring, smart design, and cross-sector governance to restore urban ecological synchrony.

science.title: One-way quantum synchronization could make quantum computers more reliable
science.description: Scientists at RIKEN have proposed a new way to make quantum systems synchronize in only one direction—like a one-way street for sound particles known as phonons. The breakthrough combines two quantum effects to create a form of one-way quantum synchronization that remains surprisingly stable even when exposed to manufacturing flaws and environmental noise, two major obstacles that have long hindered real-world quantum technologies.

science.title: Ancient DNA shared with Neanderthals may explain human language
science.description: A tiny set of ancient genetic “switches” may have played a surprisingly large role in making human language possible.
